subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should OpenClaw add a public binding-scoped tool-policy contract for route and ACP bindings, or should operators use the existing group/sender/session policy surfaces instead?
rationale: This is a new security-control config surface; automation cannot choose the permanent precedence and ownership model without maintainer intent.

options.title: Implement binding policy end to end
options.body: Add `bindings[].tools` only with typed schema, route/ACP propagation, enforcement in every tool preparation path, docs, and upgrade/security tests.

options.title: Use existing scoped policy
options.body: Keep `bindings[]` routing-only and document channel group, sender, and session policy as the supported way to restrict tools by conversation.

options.title: Fold into broader session policy
options.body: Defer this exact config key and resolve it through the broader per-session or conversation identity work instead.

recommendation.title: Implement binding policy end to end
recommendation.body: Add `bindings[].tools` only with typed schema, route/ACP propagation, enforcement in every tool preparation path, docs, and upgrade/security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent scoped conversation capability profile work is the likely foundation for a single owner decision across route, ACP, and runtime tool policy.
